replication.target_description: Experiment 1: self-reported right-handed participants judged whether the right or left hand was larger. Two goodness-of-fit tests are reported: initial directional responses and all responses after the forced-choice follow-up. The locator does not identify which test is intended; the supplied description says length while this experiment measures categorical perceived overall hand size.

n.sample_role: Candidate analytic participant counts: N = 35 for initial directional responses; N = 50 including forced-choice follow-up responses. No unique target analytic N selected.
n.exclusions: First analysis omits the 15 initially same-size responses; second includes their follow-up choices. No further exclusions stated for these analyses.

notes: Identity independently supported by the canonical text header: title “It’s Out of My Hands! Grasping Capacity May Not Influence Perceived Object Size”, authors Elizabeth S Collier and Rebecca Lawson, journal 43(4):749–769 (2017), DOI 10.1037/xhp0000331. The supplied candidate is a primary full-article PMC HTML parse with Methods, Results, appendices and references, rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF was supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed. Only n_r and es_value_r are assigned; all other fields are placeholders. Target ambiguity: both initial-response and inclusive forced-choice tests address perceived right-versus-left hand size in Experiment 1; neither study identifier nor p. 751 locator distinguishes them. Candidate test 1: printed N = 35, χ²(1, N = 35) = 6.4, p < .001; initial right n = 25 and left n = 10. Candidate test 2: printed N = 50, χ²(1, N = 50) = 15.7, p < .001; includes additional right n = 14 and left n = 1 from the forced-choice follow-up. Both same-test printed p bounds retained here without selecting a target. N values are directly printed, not derived from df or recruitment total; no analytic N sum is adopted. The neutral description specifies hand length, whereas the replication asks which hand is bigger; this wording difference is retained. Do not select a candidate by numeric matching.
